scope: Completed 350-year long-healing case, eight individual panels, and Supplementary Figures 3 and 4 composites; this record makes no global completion or convergence claim.
checks: Successful completed run, source/executable/configuration hashes, archived configuration, end time and mesh.
Finite complete history, consecutive accepted steps, increasing time, consistent step durations and accepted errors at most one.
Positive effective stress, permeability bounds and whole-history resolution minima.
Complete binary records, mesh coordinates, finite fields and exact saved time/step agreement with history.
Positive saved stress, constitutive permeability bounds and permeability no greater than reference permeability.
Effective stress constant in every fixed-pressure saved profile when that option is enabled.
All eight NPZ arrays exactly match selected time, depth, accepted step and field values from the independently generated binary output.
Profile times, values and classes match the documented four-year interseismic, one-year early stress, and one-second coseismic selections.
Cumulative slip starts from the first selected snapshot; S3d retains the last two complete large-event cycles.
Complete-cycle bounds are independently derived from the complete-event catalog; all recurrence intervals, last interval and median are retained.
Panel source, executable, configuration, pipeline hashes and commands agree with the current files.
All plotted floating-point arrays are finite, and individual dataset and figure files are smaller than 100 MiB.

findings: Panel labels, units, legends, ticks and color scales are present and legible. The stress-profile depth label was confirmed in both PNG and PDF.

S3c shows a deep partial rupture followed by a surface-reaching large event, but does not recover the same sequence of arrested fronts visible in the published step map. Equivalent published event boundaries are unspecified, so one-to-one event identities are not assigned.

The resolved partial rupture peaks 55.70 years after cycle opening; its connected >=1 cm footprint spans 14.06--16.90 km. The closing large event first crosses the speed threshold near 13.51 km depth. These are calculated diagnostics, not digitized published nucleation depths.

The selected final cycle lasts 70.46 years, about 8.4 percent longer than the approximately 65-year published example. The median of all five intervals is 63.57 years; it is not substituted for the displayed final cycle or treated as a stationary period.

S3d shows two complete cycles. The final shallowest cumulative slip of 6.96 m has a similar scale to the approximately 7 m published panel; this visual scale comparison does not establish curve agreement. The maximum final slip is 7.52 m.

Saved-profile cadence produces steps in the accepted-step map; accepted step count is not a physical accuracy metric. The selected maps end at the closing earthquake, whereas the published maps include a post-earthquake tail.

S4 shows stress, permeability and flux cycling. At the sampled depth near 10 km, stress spans 16.51 MPa, permeability varies by a factor of approximately 9.64, and flux ranges from 1.50e-9 to 1.58e-8 m/s. The maximum effective stress occurs 34.41 years after cycle opening.

Leading and deepest contour migration medians are 186.88 and 241.81 m/yr, compared with the printed 120 m/yr. The individual 125.95 m/yr segment is retained with all other segments rather than used as the overall migration rate.
The minimum frictional nucleation length spans 4.96 cells. No separate spatial refinement sequence is available for this healing time; all eight panels remain partial.
